title: Why Tejal Patwardhan stopped underestimating the models - Episode 21
description: The old tests are getting too easy. Tejal Patwardhan leads OpenAI’s frontier evals team, which is finding new ways to measure and forecast progress as models become more capable. She and host Andrew Mayne discuss why evals matter for research, how benchmarks can break or get gamed, and what models need to be judged on next.

segments.heading: Core Architecture and Technical Motivations for Why Tejal Patwardhan stopped underestimating the models - Episode 21
segments.text: In this session on Why Tejal Patwardhan stopped underestimating the models - Episode 21, Tejal Patwardhan, Andrew Mayne examine the underlying architectural principles and operational requirements shaping frontier AI systems. The presentation highlights how modern engineering teams leverage OpenAI, Frontier Evals, Reasoning Benchmarks to address foundational challenges in Research/Papers, LLM Fundamentals. Rather than relying on rigid heuristic pipelines, the architecture emphasizes end-to-end model legibility, structured context windows, and robust feedback loops. Participants explore how these patterns eliminate brittle manual glue code, providing a resilient platform capable of maintaining accuracy even under intense compute constraints and rapid requirement iteration.

segments.heading: Operational Deployment, Evaluation Benchmarks, and Future Trajectory
segments.text: The concluding segment addresses enterprise deployment standards, cost efficiency trade-offs, and empirical evaluation benchmarks. Looking ahead, the discussion outlines upcoming platform milestones and strategic paradigms for scaling autonomous, high-integrity AI workloads across diverse industry domains.
